questions.question_text: A circle has diameter $PQ$ and centre $(0, 2)$. One end of the diameter is $P(3, 5)$. Find the coordinates of $Q$.

options.why: Found the midpoint of the centre and $P$ instead of treating the centre as the midpoint of $PQ$.
Solved the $x$-coordinate correctly but used $y_Q = -y_P$ rather than $y_Q = 2(2) - 5$.
Left $x_Q$ equal to $x_P$, not solving $\frac{3+x_Q}{2}=0$ for the missing coordinate.

questions.solution_text:
The centre is the midpoint of diameter $PQ$.
$\dfrac{3 + x_Q}{2} = 0$
$3 + x_Q = 0$
$x_Q = -3$
$\dfrac{5 + y_Q}{2} = 2$
$5 + y_Q = 4$
$y_Q = -1$
$Q = (-3, -1)$
